name: TurboQuant KV Cache
intro:
Measured allocation, total Metal memory,
and what a one-million-token projection cannot say.
version: Repository experiment · protocol and interpretation limits in the full report

chapters.title:
Quantize the cache.
Measure the process.
chapters.subtitle: Q8 keys and TurboQuant 4-bit values.
paragraphs: This local lab compares FP16 K/V with Q8_0 keys plus TurboQuant 4-bit values on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct Q8_0, running on an M1 Max. All prompts are synthetic.
Only values use TurboQuant here. This setup differs from Google’s research evaluation and should be interpreted as a local implementation experiment.
chapters.note: The source report records configured capacity separately from input-token count.

chapters.title:
896 MiB.
357 MiB.
chapters.subtitle: The same measured input length.
paragraphs: At 30,290 input tokens and a configured capacity of 32,768, FP16 KV allocation is 896 MiB and the experimental format uses 357 MiB, a 60.2% reduction.
The measured points are separate process runs with capacity reserved by the backend. They do not depict a single process’s cache growing live.
chapters.note: The shorter point is a median across four prompts; the longer points are medians across two.

chapters.title:
The cache is
part of the total.
chapters.subtitle: Weights and compute buffers remain.
paragraphs: At 30.3k input tokens, the experimental total Metal allocation is 3,829 MiB: 1,801 MiB model weights, 1,671 MiB compute buffers, and 357 MiB KV.
The FP16 total is 4,368 MiB. Its 896 MiB KV allocation is only one segment. RSS is a separate process-memory measurement and must not be added to Metal allocation.
chapters.note: The 60.2% cache reduction is not a 60.2% reduction in total memory.

chapters.title:
Memory saved.
More time to prefill.
chapters.subtitle: Read retrieval and latency together.
paragraphs: At 30.3k, median prefill was 37.74 s with FP16 and 73.09 s with the experimental format. FP16 returned the first target code in both cases; the experimental format succeeded in one of two.
The short-context runs were more favorable, but two long-context cases and a single run per condition cannot estimate general retrieval accuracy.
chapters.note: The result is a local memory–latency–retrieval trade-off, not a universal quality guarantee.

chapters.title:
Estimate storage.
Do not invent a run.
chapters.subtitle: One million allocated tokens is arithmetic.
paragraphs: Keeping this architecture and cache format fixed, the two longer capacities imply 28 KiB per allocated token for FP16 and about 11.16 KiB for the experimental format.
At one million allocated tokens, those rates project about 26.7 GiB versus 10.6 GiB of KV storage. This model’s native context limit is 32,768, so these are not executable one-million-token results.
chapters.note: The estimate says nothing about one-million-token accuracy, prefill time, temporary memory, or total Metal allocation.
